macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Global stocks rise as softer U.S. data eases Fed hike fears
items.summary: Asian shares rose and U.S. equity futures edged higher as investors scaled back expectations for a near-term Federal Reserve rate hike after softer U.S. data, including weaker retail sales and cooler inflation readings. The dollar slipped toward recent lows while Treasury yields eased, reinforcing the view that policy rates may stay unchanged in the near term.

items.title: Major U.S. stock indexes close at or near records on easing rate fears
items.summary: The S&P 500 and Russell 2000 closed at record highs, while the Nasdaq also remained near records as investors welcomed signs that the Fed is less likely to tighten policy soon. Broader risk sentiment improved despite lingering concerns that weaker economic data could signal slowing growth.

items.title: Asia-Pacific markets mostly higher; Japan, Hong Kong and Shanghai advance
items.summary: Asian markets traded higher, with Japan’s Nikkei up 0.7%, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng up 1.3%, and Shanghai’s Composite up 1.4%. European futures also firmed, reflecting improved risk appetite after U.S. inflation and labor data reduced pressure on the Federal Reserve to raise rates soon.

items.title: Dollar weakens as traders pare back Fed rate-hike bets
items.summary: The U.S. dollar eased against major currencies, with the dollar index near its lowest levels of the month and the yen strengthening. Markets now see a much lower probability of a Fed rate hike next month, with traders awaiting the Jackson Hole symposium for clearer policy signals.

items.title: Oil prices and bond yields move lower amid softer growth signals
items.summary: West Texas Intermediate and Brent crude both fell, while U.S. Treasury yields slipped after mixed trading last week. The move reflected a combination of easing Fed-tightening fears and concerns that weakening U.S. data may point to slower growth ahead.

items.title: Fed watch: markets increasingly expect rates to stay steady
items.summary: Traders have sharply reduced bets on a near-term Fed hike after July retail sales unexpectedly fell and consumer sentiment weakened. Market pricing has shifted toward a high likelihood that the central bank will hold rates at its next meeting, with few fresh clues expected before Jackson Hole.

items.title: Soft U.S. inflation and retail sales data support equity rally
items.summary: Inflation cooled and retail sales weakened, helping fuel a rally in U.S. stocks as investors interpreted the data as reducing the chance of further Fed tightening. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq had recently hit record levels, supported in part by lower rate fears and strong positioning in growth stocks.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin rebounds near $64,000 after a selloff, with ETF flows and macro fears still driving volatility
items.summary: Bitcoin recovered to around the mid-$64,000 range after a recent AI-led crypto rout, while other coverage says it is still consolidating near $62,000-$63,000 as investors weigh inflation, geopolitical tensions, and ETF outflows. Several market trackers also show Bitcoin and Ethereum only modestly changed over 24 hours, underscoring a choppy trading environment.

items.title: Bitcoin ETF activity draws attention as institutional demand remains a major market driver
items.summary: Crypto market coverage highlighted a surge in Bitcoin ETF interest, including reporting that a Bitcoin ETF saw a $371 million inflow surge. At the same time, other reports noted ongoing ETF outflows, suggesting institutional flows remain mixed and are still influencing short-term price action.

items.title: Ethereum and major altcoins trade mixed as the market stays cautious
items.summary: Market snapshots showed Ethereum hovering around the high-$1,800s to about $1,910, while XRP, Solana, and Dogecoin posted small gains or losses. The broader market remains in sideways consolidation, with total crypto market capitalization down slightly in some trackers.

items.title: Dutch prosecutors sell seized Knaken crypto for €2.2 million after exchange bankruptcy
items.summary: Dutch prosecutors sold seized cryptocurrency tied to Knaken for €2.2 million after the exchange went bankrupt. The move is part of a broader set of insolvency and asset-recovery developments affecting creditors.

items.title: Bitpanda fined €70,000 by Austrian regulator over MiCA breaches
items.summary: Austria’s regulator fined Bitpanda €70,000 for breaches related to MiCA compliance. The case adds to the ongoing wave of European enforcement as exchanges adapt to the bloc’s crypto rulebook.

items.title: Harmony plans chain rollback after forged ONE tokens spread across the network
items.summary: Harmony said it is preparing a chain rollback after forged ONE tokens spread across the network. The incident is notable because rollback proposals in public blockchains are rare and can affect confidence in network finality.

items.title: Ripple mints 10 million RLUSD as supply reaches 1.71 billion
items.summary: Ripple minted another 10 million RLUSD, bringing the stablecoin’s supply to 1.71 billion. The expansion indicates continued activity around Ripple’s dollar-backed token and related payment infrastructure.

items.title: Blockstream launches swaps service after Boltz suspends operations
items.summary: Blockstream introduced a swaps service after Boltz suspended operations. The development is relevant for users seeking bitcoin-native exchange and liquidity tools amid shifting service availability in the ecosystem.

items.title: China adds eight banks to its digital yuan network
items.summary: China expanded its digital yuan network by adding eight more banks, bringing the number of operators to 30. The move reflects continued state-backed development of China’s central bank digital currency infrastructure.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Fortnite teases major crossover season with Sonic, Crash, Mega Man, and more
items.summary: Fortnite’s next season, titled "Override," is being promoted as a large crossover event featuring many iconic video game characters, including Sonic, Crash Bandicoot, Mega Man, and Sora. The season is set to launch on August 20.

items.title: Senate subcommittee opens investigation into Roblox child safety
items.summary: A U.S. Senate subcommittee has launched an investigation into Roblox, citing concerns that the platform prioritizes revenue and engagement over child safety. The inquiry follows allegations of criminal activity on the service.

items.title: Netflix is shutting down two game studios
items.summary: Netflix is closing two of its game studios, including Night School Studio, the developer behind Oxenfree and Unhinged. The move comes despite recent praise for the studio’s work.

items.title: Alibaba sells gaming business Lingxi as it pivots toward AI and e-commerce
items.summary: Alibaba is divesting its videogame business, Lingxi Games, in a deal reportedly worth at least $1.5 billion. The sale is part of the company’s broader shift in focus toward artificial intelligence and e-commerce.

items.title: Esports World Cup 2026 sees Team Falcons extend Club Championship lead
items.summary: Team Falcons continued its surge in the Esports World Cup 2026 Club Championship after securing a Rocket League victory. The result strengthens its position in the overall standings.

items.title: New Japanese game releases include Starsand Island and STEINS;GATE RE:BOOT
items.summary: This week’s Japanese release lineup is led by Starsand Island and STEINS;GATE RE:BOOT, with Mortal Shell II and Dungeon Antiqua 2 also among the notable launches. Several of the titles span multiple platforms, including Switch 2, PS5, Xbox Series, and PC.

items.title: Apple and MLB bring live baseball games to Vision Pro
items.summary: Apple and Major League Baseball announced that live games will begin streaming on Vision Pro starting August 28. The move expands the headset’s sports viewing lineup.

items.title: Meta cuts Beat Saber price and announces new smartglasses grants
items.summary: Meta lowered the price of Beat Saber from $29.99 to $19.99. The company also published a list of 30 U.S. entities receiving grants for smartglasses-related projects.
